issue.title: Assertion failure in Modules/_io/textio.c `_io_TextIOWrapper_tell_impl: Assertion 'skip_back <= PyBytes_GET_SIZE(next_input)' failed`

labels.name: extension-modules
labels.description: C modules in the Modules dir

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

```python
import io
import os
from test.support import os_helper

DATA_TEMPLATE = ['line1=1']
DATA_CR = r'\n\r\t'.join(DATA_TEMPLATE) + '\r'

open_func = io.open

READMODE = 'r'
WRITEMODE = 'wb'

data = DATA_CR
if 'b' in WRITEMODE:
    data = data.encode('ascii')

with open_func(os_helper.TESTFN, WRITEMODE) as fp:
    fp.write(data)

with open_func(os_helper.TESTFN, READMODE) as fp:
    _ = fp.readline()
    pos = fp.tell()
```

```
python: ../Modules/_io/textio.c:2848: _io_TextIOWrapper_tell_impl: Assertion `skip_back <= PyBytes_GET_SIZE(next_input)' failed.
Aborted (core dumped)
```


### CPython versions tested on:

CPython main branch

### Operating systems tested on:

Linux

comments.body:
Smaller repro:
```py
import io
data = b'line1=1\r'
with open('s', 'wb') as fp:
    fp.write(data)
with open('s', 'r') as fp:
    fp.readline()
    fp.tell()
```

@StanFromIreland , Thanks, I reproduced this issue, and I think the assertion failure occurs because the tell() method's optimization algorithm assumes there's buffered input data to search through, but when a file ends with a standalone carriage return (\r), an empty snapshot buffer gets created. The algorithm calculates that it needs to skip some bytes based on the character-to-byte ratio, then tries to navigate within the buffer using a binary search approach, but fails when skip_back=1 exceeds the buffer size of 0. I think the cleanest fix is to detect when next_input is empty and skip the optimization phase entirely, letting the algorithm fall back to the precise byte-by-byte decoding method, which always works correctly. I can open the PR if this seems correct.
Happy for others to work on, planning to look at myself no earlier than next Tuesday. I've mainly been focusing on BufferdIO which sits below TextIO so not sure the likely code changes needed here.
